questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: An enterprise runs a mission-critical legacy web application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk using a custom platform. The engineering team must implement a deployment strategy that guarantees zero downtime, maintains 100% compute capacity during the deployment, and allows for an instant, near-zero seconds rollback mechanism if critical production errors are detected. Which deployment strategy meets these stringent requirements with the LEAST operational impact to active users?

options.text: Configure the Elastic Beanstalk environment to use the Immutable deployment policy, which provisions a temporary Auto Scaling group for the new version and seamlessly swaps the instances behind the existing load balancer.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Immutable deployments maintain 100% capacity and are safe, a rollback requires terminating the new instances or redeploying the old version, which is not an instant process.

options.text: Configure the Elastic Beanstalk environment to use the Rolling with Additional Batch deployment policy to ensure capacity never drops below 100% while gradually updating instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Rolling with Additional Batch maintains capacity but updating instances takes time, and rolling back would require a reverse rolling deployment, taking significant time.

options.text: Provision a completely separate new Elastic Beanstalk environment running the new application version, perform validation tests, and execute an Elastic Beanstalk CNAME swap to instantly redirect traffic.
options.explanation: Correct: A Blue/Green deployment via CNAME swap provides zero capacity degradation during deployment and allows an instant rollback by simply swapping the CNAMEs back in DNS.

options.text: Implement a Canary deployment strategy using AWS CodeDeploy integrated directly with Elastic Beanstalk, shifting 10% of the traffic initially and automatically rolling back upon CloudWatch alarm triggers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Elastic Beanstalk does not natively support AWS CodeDeploy Canary deployments in this manner. CodeDeploy is for EC2/ECS/Lambda natively, while EB has its own deployment mechanisms.

questions.generalExplanation: For Elastic Beanstalk applications requiring zero downtime, 100% capacity, and instant rollback capabilities, the Blue/Green deployment strategy utilizing the CNAME swap feature is the only architecture that fully satisfies all constraints.

pt.statement: Uma empresa executa uma aplicação web legada de missão crítica no AWS Elastic Beanstalk usando uma plataforma personalizada. A equipe de engenharia deve implementar uma estratégia de implantação que garanta tempo de inatividade zero, mantenha 100% da capacidade de computação durante a implantação e permita um mecanismo de reversão instantâneo (rollback) de quase zero segundos caso erros críticos de produção sejam detectados. Qual estratégia de implantação atende a esses rigorosos requisitos com o MENOR impacto operacional para os usuários ativos?

options.text: Configurar o ambiente do Elastic Beanstalk para usar a política de implantação Imutável (Immutable), que provisiona um Auto Scaling group temporário para a nova versão e troca perfeitamente as instâncias atrás do balanceador de carga existente.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Embora as implantações imutáveis mantenham 100% da capacidade e sejam seguras, uma reversão exige o encerramento das novas instâncias ou a reimplantação da versão antiga, o que não é um processo instantâneo.

options.text: Configurar o ambiente do Elastic Beanstalk para usar a política de implantação Contínua com Lote Adicional (Rolling with Additional Batch) para garantir que a capacidade nunca caia abaixo de 100% enquanto atualiza gradualmente as instâncias.
options.explanation: Incorreto: A implantação contínua com lote adicional mantém a capacidade, mas a atualização das instâncias leva tempo, e a reversão exigiria uma implantação contínua reversa, consumindo tempo significativo.

options.text: Provisionar um ambiente Elastic Beanstalk totalmente separado executando a nova versão da aplicação, realizar testes de validação e executar uma troca de CNAME do Elastic Beanstalk para redirecionar instantaneamente o tráfego.
options.explanation: Correto: Uma implantação Blue/Green por meio da troca de CNAME fornece zero degradação de capacidade durante a implantação e permite uma reversão instantânea simplesmente trocando os CNAMEs de volta no DNS.

options.text: Implementar uma estratégia de implantação Canary usando o AWS CodeDeploy integrado diretamente ao Elastic Beanstalk, transferindo 10% do tráfego inicialmente e revertendo automaticamente em caso de acionamento de alarmes do CloudWatch.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O Elastic Beanstalk não suporta nativamente implantações Canary do AWS CodeDeploy dessa maneira. O CodeDeploy é para EC2/ECS/Lambda nativamente, enquanto o EB possui seus próprios mecanismos de implantação.

pt.generalExplanation: Para aplicações no Elastic Beanstalk que exigem tempo de inatividade zero, 100% de capacidade e recursos de reversão instantânea, a estratégia de implantação Blue/Green utilizando o recurso de troca de CNAME é a única arquitetura que satisfaz totalmente todas as restrições.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A globally distributed enterprise manages a fleet of 5,000 Amazon EC2 instances and 1,000 on-premises servers running a mix of Windows Server and Amazon Linux 2. The security team mandates a strict patch compliance process where all critical OS updates must be automatically applied within 48 hours of release, specifically during predefined regional maintenance windows. Any non-compliant instances must be immediately identified without requiring SSH or RDP access. Which combination of actions should the Solutions Architect take to implement this architecture with minimal operational overhead? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Deploy AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) to all on-premises servers using managed instance activations, ensuring the EC2 instances have the appropriate IAM instance profiles attached to communicate with the Systems Manager service.
options.explanation: Correct: Hybrid environments require the SSM Agent installed on on-premises servers via managed instance activations, and EC2 instances must possess the necessary IAM role to authorize API communication.

options.text: Establish a Site-to-Site VPN to push patches from an on-premises WSUS server to EC2 instances, while utilizing AWS Systems Manager Run Command for the on-premises Linux instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Utilizing an on-premises WSUS server for EC2 instances increases operational overhead and creates a fragmented patching strategy compared to a unified AWS Systems Manager approach.

options.text: Create custom AWS Systems Manager Patch Baselines for Windows and Linux that explicitly approve critical updates. Associate these baselines with Patch Groups defined by resource tags, and schedule them within Systems Manager Maintenance Windows.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager utilizes Patch Baselines and Patch Groups (via tags) to automate patch installation within specific Maintenance Windows across heterogeneous hybrid fleets.

options.text: Use AWS CodeDeploy with a custom appspec.yml file to execute shell scripts on all instances to fetch and install OS packages, scheduled via Amazon EventBridge cron expressions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS CodeDeploy is designed for application code deployment, not fleet-wide operating system patching. It lacks the compliance reporting and baseline features native to SSM Patch Manager.

options.text: Configure AWS OpsWorks Stacks to orchestrate Chef recipes that download and install critical OS patches across the hybrid fleet during off-peak hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS OpsWorks reached its End-of-Life (EOL) in May 2024 and is no longer a viable or recommended service for modern fleet automation and patch management.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Systems Manager natively handles hybrid patch management. On-premises servers are onboarded via managed instance activations (SSM Agent), and EC2 instances use IAM instance profiles. Patch Baselines automate critical update approvals, mapped to Patch Groups and executed within Maintenance Windows.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: An enterprise is modernizing an on-premises monolithic application by migrating it to a containerized microservices architecture on Amazon ECS using AWS Fargate. During the deployment of new container images, the company requires strict validation testing. Traffic must be shifted precisely in 10% increments every 5 minutes. If an elevated HTTP 5XX error rate is detected by Amazon CloudWatch, the deployment must automatically halt and roll back completely to the previous version without any manual intervention. Which implementation satisfies these specific routing and automation requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CodeDeploy configured with an ECS compute platform. Define an appspec.yaml specifying the task definition and use the CodeDeployDefault.ECSLinear10PercentEvery5Minutes deployment configuration, linking the CloudWatch alarm in the CodeDeploy deployment group for automatic rollbacks.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS CodeDeploy supports natively the ECS platform and provides Linear and Canary deployment configurations. Linking CloudWatch alarms enables automated rollbacks.

options.text: Use Amazon ECS rolling updates by updating the service's minimum healthy percent to 100% and maximum percent to 200%. Configure a CloudWatch Events rule to trigger an AWS Lambda function that reverts the task definition if 5XX errors exceed the threshold.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ECS standard rolling updates cannot natively perform linear traffic shifting in exact percentages over specific time intervals, nor do they natively hook into CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollbacks without writing custom Lambda automation code.

options.text: Implement AWS CodePipeline with AWS CloudFormation. Use the AWS::ECS::Service resource with a UpdatePolicy set to AutoScalingRollingUpdate and integrate the Application Load Balancer target group weights to shift 10% every 5 minutes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS CloudFormation AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy applies to EC2 Auto Scaling groups, not ECS services or ALB target group weighting.

options.text: Configure an Application Load Balancer with a weighted target group rule. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine that updates the ALB weights by 10% every 5 minutes and uses a Catch block to revert weights if the CloudWatch alarm fires.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While technically possible with extensive custom development, this approach introduces significant operational overhead and is suboptimal compared to using AWS CodeDeploy's native, out-of-the-box linear shifting capabilities.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS CodeDeploy for Amazon ECS natively supports Blue/Green, Canary, and Linear deployments. By specifying the `CodeDeployDefault.ECSLinear10PercentEvery5Minutes` configuration and attaching CloudWatch alarms to the CodeDeploy Deployment Group, automatic traffic shifting and rollback are fully managed without custom scripts.

questions.statement: An organization relies heavily on AWS CodeBuild to compile code and produce Docker container images. During a recent audit, the security team discovered that several developers had accidentally hardcoded third-party API keys within their application source code, pushing them to CodeCommit. To mitigate this risk, the architecture team wants to extract these keys into a centralized secure store and dynamically inject them into the container build environment ONLY during the AWS CodeBuild execution phase. The solution must strictly prevent the keys from appearing in CloudWatch Logs or being exposed in the final Docker image. Which configuration achieves these requirements with the HIGHEST security?

options.text: Store the API keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString. In the buildspec.yml file, define the parameters in the 'env:parameter-store' section. Pass them as standard build arguments using '--build-arg' to the Docker build command, ensuring they are scrubbed after.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Passing sensitive data using standard Docker '--build-arg' bakes the secrets into the image's intermediate layers, exposing them to anyone with access to the final image.

options.text: Store the API keys in AWS Secrets Manager. Update the buildspec.yml to retrieve the secrets in the 'env:secrets-manager' section. Mount the secrets as temporary files during the Docker build using Docker BuildKit's secret mounting feature ('--mount=type=secret').
options.explanation: Correct: Retrieving secrets via CodeBuild 'env:secrets-manager' protects them in transit, and using Docker BuildKit's '--mount=type=secret' feature ensures that the secrets are injected only for the build process without ever being persisted in the Docker image layers or history.

options.text: Encrypt the API keys using AWS KMS and store the ciphertext in the source repository. Use AWS CodeBuild 'pre_build' commands to decrypt the payload using the AWS CLI and export them as standard environment variables for the build process.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exporting secrets as standard environment variables can inadvertently leak them into CloudWatch Logs if the build process prints the environment, and they may be captured in the Docker history.

options.text: Configure an AWS Lambda function to rotate the API keys and push them to an Amazon S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-S3. Grant the CodeBuild IAM service role access to the S3 bucket to download the keys into the workspace root directory.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Downloading secrets into the CodeBuild workspace root directory risks baking the files directly into the Docker image when the 'COPY . .' command is executed during the build.

questions.generalExplanation: To maintain zero-trust security during CI/CD pipelines, secrets must not be stored in source code or intermediate Docker layers. By defining secrets in the `env:secrets-manager` section of the `buildspec.yml`, AWS CodeBuild safely resolves them. Passing them via Docker BuildKit secret mounts (`--mount=type=secret`) ensures the container process can access them during compilation, but they are never committed to the image layers.

options.A: Deploy AWS Lake Formation in a centralized data account and register the S3 buckets from all 50 accounts as data lake locations. Configure a central AWS Glue Data Catalog and share it with the 50 consumer accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Define row-level and column-level access policies centrally in Lake Formation. Instruct analysts to query the data using Athena from their respective accounts.
options.B: Configure AWS Glue Crawlers in each of the 50 accounts to build local Glue Data Catalogs. Establish cross-account IAM roles to allow a central account's Amazon Athena to query the distributed buckets. Implement S3 bucket policies with conditions to enforce row-level and column-level security. Use AWS RAM to share the S3 endpoints.
options.C: Provision a central Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Ranger enabled. Use AWS Glue ETL jobs to continuously extract data from the 50 accounts and load it into a central S3 bucket in Apache Parquet format. Configure Ranger to enforce row-level and column-level security. Analysts connect to EMR via JDBC to run queries.
options.D: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster in a central account. Use Redshift Spectrum to query the S3 data directly across the 50 accounts by assuming cross-account IAM roles. Implement Redshift row-level security (RLS) policies and column-level grants.

en.explanation: Option A is correct because AWS Lake Formation natively supports centralized, fine-grained access control (row and column-level) for data in Amazon S3, minimizing both data duplication and operational overhead. Option B is incorrect as S3 bucket policies and IAM cannot natively enforce row or column-level security. Option C duplicates data and introduces the massive overhead of managing EMR clusters. Option D is less efficient for direct S3 querying and requires heavy IAM role management compared to Lake Formation.

pt.scenario: Uma empresa financeira global possui dados distribuídos em buckets do Amazon S3 em 50 contas da AWS. A organização deseja estabelecer um data lake centralizado para permitir que analistas de dados executem consultas SQL usando o Amazon Athena. O diretor de segurança determina que controles de acesso refinados, especificamente segurança em nível de linha e de coluna, devem ser aplicados globalmente com base nas personas dos usuários. A solução deve minimizar a duplicação de dados e a sobrecarga operacional.
pt.question: Qual arquitetura atenderá a esses requisitos de forma MAIS eficiente?

options.A: Implante o AWS Lake Formation em uma conta de dados centralizada e registre os buckets do S3 de todas as 50 contas como locais do data lake. Configure um AWS Glue Data Catalog central e compartilhe-o com as 50 contas consumidoras usando o AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Defina as políticas de acesso em nível de linha e de coluna centralmente no Lake Formation. Instrua os analistas a consultar os dados usando o Athena a partir de suas respectivas contas.
options.B: Configure os AWS Glue Crawlers em cada uma das 50 contas para criar Glue Data Catalogs locais. Estabeleça funções (roles) do IAM entre contas para permitir que o Amazon Athena de uma conta central consulte os buckets distribuídos. Implemente políticas de bucket do S3 com condições para aplicar segurança em nível de linha e coluna. Use o AWS RAM para compartilhar os endpoints do S3.
options.C: Provisione um cluster Amazon EMR central com o Apache Ranger ativado. Use trabalhos de ETL do AWS Glue para extrair continuamente dados das 50 contas e carregá-los em um bucket S3 central no formato Apache Parquet. Configure o Ranger para aplicar a segurança em nível de linha e coluna. Os analistas se conectam ao EMR via JDBC para executar consultas.
options.D: Crie um cluster do Amazon Redshift em uma conta central. Use o Redshift Spectrum para consultar os dados do S3 diretamente nas 50 contas assumindo roles do IAM entre contas. Implemente políticas de segurança em nível de linha (RLS) do Redshift e concessões em nível de coluna.

pt.explanation: A opção A é correta porque o AWS Lake Formation suporta nativamente o controle de acesso centralizado e refinado (nível de linha e coluna) para dados no Amazon S3, minimizando a duplicação de dados e a sobrecarga operacional. A opção B é incorreta porque políticas de bucket e IAM não podem aplicar nativamente segurança em nível de linha ou coluna para consultas do Athena. A opção C duplica dados e introduz a sobrecarga de gerenciamento de clusters EMR e Apache Ranger. A opção D requer gerenciamento pesado de permissões cruzadas no IAM em comparação com o Lake Formation.

es.scenario: Una empresa financiera global tiene datos distribuidos en buckets de Amazon S3 en 50 cuentas de AWS. La organización desea establecer un lago de datos centralizado para permitir a los analistas de datos ejecutar consultas SQL utilizando Amazon Athena. El director de seguridad exige que se apliquen controles de acceso detallados, específicamente seguridad a nivel de fila y de columna, a nivel global según los perfiles de los usuarios. La solución debe minimizar la duplicación de datos y la sobrecarga operativa.
es.question: ¿Qué arquitectura cumplirá con estos requisitos de la manera MÁS eficiente?

options.A: Implemente AWS Lake Formation en una cuenta de datos centralizada y registre los buckets de S3 de las 50 cuentas como ubicaciones del lago de datos. Configure un catálogo de datos central de AWS Glue y compártalo con las 50 cuentas consumidoras mediante AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Defina políticas de acceso a nivel de fila y columna centralmente en Lake Formation. Indique a los analistas que consulten los datos utilizando Athena desde sus respectivas cuentas.
options.B: Configure AWS Glue Crawlers en cada una de las 50 cuentas para crear catálogos de datos locales de Glue. Establezca roles de IAM entre cuentas para permitir que Amazon Athena de una cuenta central consulte los buckets distribuidos. Implemente políticas de bucket de S3 con condiciones para aplicar seguridad a nivel de fila y columna. Utilice AWS RAM para compartir los puntos de enlace de S3.
options.C: Aprovisione un clúster central de Amazon EMR con Apache Ranger habilitado. Utilice trabajos de ETL de AWS Glue para extraer continuamente datos de las 50 cuentas y cargarlos en un bucket de S3 central en formato Apache Parquet. Configure Ranger para aplicar seguridad a nivel de fila y columna. Los analistas se conectan a EMR a través de JDBC para ejecutar consultas.
options.D: Cree un clúster de Amazon Redshift en una cuenta central. Utilice Redshift Spectrum para consultar los datos de S3 directamente en las 50 cuentas asumiendo roles de IAM entre cuentas. Implemente políticas de seguridad a nivel de fila (RLS) de Redshift y concesiones a nivel de columna.

es.explanation: La opción A es correcta porque AWS Lake Formation admite de forma nativa el control de acceso centralizado y detallado (nivel de fila y columna) para datos en Amazon S3, lo que minimiza tanto la duplicación de datos como la sobrecarga operativa. La opción B es incorrecta porque las políticas de bucket y de IAM no pueden aplicar de forma nativa seguridad a nivel de fila o columna. La opción C duplica datos e introduce sobrecarga en la administración de EMR. La opción D es menos eficiente y requiere una gran administración de roles de IAM.

en.scenario: A healthcare call center records thousands of customer support calls daily, storing the audio files in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect must design a serverless workflow to generate text transcripts of these calls, extract customer sentiment, and identify key phrases. Before the transcripts can be analyzed or stored in the final database, all Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI) must be strictly redacted.
en.question: Which combination of services and steps will satisfy these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure an S3 Event Notification to trigger an AWS Lambda function upon audio file upload. The Lambda function calls Amazon Transcribe to generate a transcript, then calls Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify and redact PHI/PII, and finally uses Amazon Lex to analyze sentiment before saving to Amazon DynamoDB.
options.B: Use Amazon Transcribe to convert the audio files to text. Configure an AWS Glue job to process the output files, using a custom Python script with regular expressions to find and redact PII/PHI. Finally, use Amazon Comprehend to analyze sentiment and key phrases on the redacted text, storing the results in Amazon S3.
options.C: Configure an S3 Event Notification to trigger an AWS Step Functions state machine. Use the Amazon Transcribe native integration to transcribe the audio and enable its built-in Content Redaction feature for PII. Pass the redacted transcript to Amazon Comprehend to extract sentiment and key phrases. Store the final JSON output in Amazon S3.
options.D: Process the audio files using Amazon Rekognition to extract text and analyze sentiment. Stream the output through Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, applying an inline AWS Lambda transformation function that uses Amazon Macie to redact PII from the payload before delivering the final data to Amazon OpenSearch Service.

en.explanation: Option C is correct. Amazon Transcribe has a built-in feature for PII redaction that requires no extra custom code. Amazon Comprehend natively handles sentiment analysis. Step Functions provides a fully managed serverless orchestration layer. Option A is incorrect because Lex is for building chatbots, not processing sentiment. Option B introduces high operational overhead by maintaining custom Python regex code. Option D incorrectly uses Rekognition (which is for images/video, not audio) and Macie (which scans S3, not streaming payloads).

pt.scenario: Um call center de saúde grava milhares de chamadas de suporte ao cliente diariamente, armazenando os arquivos de áudio num bucket do Amazon S3. Um arquiteto de soluções deve projetar um fluxo de trabalho serverless para gerar transcrições de texto dessas chamadas, extrair o sentimento do cliente e identificar frases-chave. Antes que as transcrições possam ser analisadas ou armazenadas no banco de dados final, todas as Informações de Identificação Pessoal (PII) e Informações de Saúde Protegidas (PHI) devem ser estritamente removidas (redacted).
pt.question: Qual combinação de serviços e etapas atenderá a esses requisitos com a MENOR sobrecarga operacional?

options.A: Configure uma notificação de evento do S3 para acionar uma função do AWS Lambda no upload do arquivo de áudio. O Lambda chama o Amazon Transcribe para gerar uma transcrição, depois chama o Amazon Comprehend Medical para redigir PHI/PII e, finalmente, usa o Amazon Lex para analisar o sentimento antes de salvar no Amazon DynamoDB.
options.B: Use o Amazon Transcribe para converter os arquivos de áudio em texto. Configure um trabalho do AWS Glue para processar os arquivos de saída, usando um script Python personalizado com expressões regulares para redigir PII/PHI. Por fim, use o Amazon Comprehend para analisar sentimentos no texto redigido, armazenando no S3.
options.C: Configure uma Notificação de Evento do S3 para acionar uma máquina de estado do AWS Step Functions. Use a integração nativa do Amazon Transcribe para transcrever o áudio e ative seu recurso integrado de Redação de Conteúdo para PII. Passe a transcrição redigida para o Amazon Comprehend extrair o sentimento e frases-chave. Armazene o JSON final no Amazon S3.
options.D: Processe os arquivos de áudio usando o Amazon Rekognition para extrair texto e analisar sentimentos. Transmita a saída por meio do Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, aplicando uma função Lambda inline que usa o Amazon Macie para redigir PII antes de entregar ao Amazon OpenSearch Service.

pt.explanation: A opção C está correta. O Amazon Transcribe possui um recurso nativo de redação de PII que não requer código personalizado. O Amazon Comprehend lida nativamente com a análise de sentimentos. A opção A está incorreta porque o Lex destina-se à criação de chatbots. A opção B introduz alta sobrecarga operacional ao manter código regex personalizado no Glue. A opção D usa incorretamente o Rekognition (que é para imagens/vídeos).

es.scenario: Un centro de llamadas de atención médica graba miles de llamadas de atención al cliente a diario, almacenando los archivos de audio en un bucket de Amazon S3. Un arquitecto de soluciones debe diseñar un flujo de trabajo sin servidor (serverless) para generar transcripciones de texto, extraer el sentimiento del cliente e identificar frases clave. Antes de que las transcripciones se puedan almacenar, toda la Información de Identificación Personal (PII) y la Información de Salud Protegida (PHI) debe redactarse de forma estricta.
es.question: ¿Qué combinación de servicios y pasos cumplirá con estos requisitos con la MENOR sobrecarga operativa?

options.A: Configure una notificación de eventos de S3 para activar una función AWS Lambda al cargar el archivo de audio. Lambda llama a Amazon Transcribe para generar la transcripción, luego a Amazon Comprehend Medical para redactar PII/PHI y usa Amazon Lex para analizar el sentimiento antes de guardar en DynamoDB.
options.B: Utilice Amazon Transcribe para convertir audio a texto. Configure un trabajo de AWS Glue con un script de Python personalizado (regex) para redactar PII/PHI. Finalmente, use Amazon Comprehend para analizar el sentimiento y frases clave, guardando en Amazon S3.
options.C: Configure una notificación de eventos de S3 para activar una máquina de estado de AWS Step Functions. Use Amazon Transcribe nativo para transcribir el audio y habilite su función integrada de redacción de contenido para PII. Pase la transcripción redactada a Amazon Comprehend para extraer el sentimiento y frases clave. Almacene el JSON final en Amazon S3.
options.D: Procese el audio con Amazon Rekognition para extraer texto y analizar sentimiento. Transmita los datos mediante Kinesis Data Firehose, aplicando una función Lambda en línea que usa Amazon Macie para redactar PII antes de enviarlos a Amazon OpenSearch.

es.explanation: La opción C es correcta. Amazon Transcribe tiene una función integrada para la redacción de PII que no requiere código adicional. Amazon Comprehend se encarga de manera nativa del análisis de sentimientos. La opción A es incorrecta porque Lex es para crear chatbots. La opción B introduce una gran sobrecarga operativa mediante código regex. La opción D utiliza incorrectamente Rekognition, que es para visión por computadora.

en.scenario: A critical financial trading application runs in the us-east-1 region. The application relies on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ database and a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The business continuity plan dictates an RPO (Recovery Point Objective) of 5 minutes and an RTO (Recovery Time Objective) of under 15 minutes in the event of a regional outage. The company wants to implement a disaster recovery strategy in us-west-2 that strictly meets these objectives while minimizing infrastructure costs when the DR site is idle.
en.question: Which combination of actions should a Solutions Architect take to implement this strategy? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Configure an Amazon RDS cross-region read replica in us-west-2. In the event of a disaster, promote the read replica to a standalone DB instance and update the application connection strings.
options.B: Enable AWS Backup to take hourly snapshots of the RDS DB instance and copy them to us-west-2. In the event of a disaster, restore the database from the latest snapshot in the DR region.
options.C: Deploy a Warm Standby architecture in us-west-2 by running a scaled-down Auto Scaling group with minimum capacity. Configure Amazon Route 53 with a failover routing policy to seamlessly redirect traffic to the ALB in us-west-2 during an outage.
options.D: Deploy a Pilot Light architecture in us-west-2 by keeping the EC2 Auto Scaling group capacity at zero. Rely on an AWS Lambda function triggered by Amazon CloudWatch alarms to scale out the instances during a disaster.
options.E: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables to ensure synchronous cross-region replication with zero data loss. Modify the application to use DynamoDB instead of PostgreSQL.

en.explanation: Options A and C are correct. The requirement is an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 15 minutes, while minimizing cost. A cross-region read replica (A) continuously asynchronously replicates data, typically providing an RPO of seconds or minutes (meeting the < 5 min RPO). A Warm Standby (C) provisions minimum necessary compute capacity that is constantly running, allowing it to take over traffic immediately via Route 53, easily satisfying the 15 min RTO. Option B (Hourly Snapshots) violates the 5-minute RPO. Option D (Pilot Light) might take longer than 15 minutes to provision instances from scratch, run init scripts, and pass health checks. Option E (DynamoDB) would require massive application refactoring and does not meet the 'minimize cost' requirement.

pt.scenario: Um aplicativo crítico de negociação financeira é executado na região us-east-1. O aplicativo depende de um banco de dados Amazon RDS para PostgreSQL Multi-AZ e de uma frota de instâncias EC2 gerenciadas por um Auto Scaling group por trás de um Application Load Balancer (ALB). O plano de continuidade de negócios dita um RPO (Recovery Point Objective) de 5 minutos e um RTO (Recovery Time Objective) de menos de 15 minutos no caso de uma interrupção regional. A empresa deseja implementar uma estratégia de recuperação de desastres (DR) em us-west-2 que atenda estritamente a esses objetivos, minimizando os custos de infraestrutura quando o local de DR estiver ocioso.
pt.question: Qual combinação de ações um Arquiteto de Soluções deve tomar para implementar essa estratégia? (Escolha DUAS.)

options.A: Configurar uma réplica de leitura de região cruzada do Amazon RDS em us-west-2. Em caso de desastre, promova a réplica de leitura para uma instância de banco de dados autônoma e atualize as strings de conexão.
options.B: Ativar o AWS Backup para tirar snapshots por hora da instância de banco de dados RDS e copiá-los para us-west-2. No caso de um desastre, restaure o banco de dados do snapshot mais recente.
options.C: Implantar uma arquitetura de Warm Standby em us-west-2 executando um Auto Scaling group reduzido com capacidade mínima. Configurar o Amazon Route 53 com uma política de roteamento de failover para o ALB em us-west-2.
options.D: Implantar uma arquitetura Pilot Light em us-west-2 mantendo a capacidade do Auto Scaling group do EC2 em zero. Depender de uma função AWS Lambda acionada por alarmes do CloudWatch para escalar as instâncias durante um desastre.
options.E: Migrar o banco de dados para o Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables para garantir replicação síncrona de região cruzada. Modificar o aplicativo para usar o DynamoDB em vez do PostgreSQL.

pt.explanation: As opções A e C estão corretas. A réplica de leitura de região cruzada (A) replica dados de forma assíncrona, normalmente fornecendo um RPO de segundos ou minutos (atendendo ao RPO de < 5 min). O Warm Standby (C) fornece capacidade de computação mínima que está constantemente em execução, satisfazendo facilmente o RTO de 15 minutos. A opção B (Snapshots por hora) viola o RPO de 5 minutos. A opção D (Pilot Light) pode demorar mais de 15 minutos para inicializar instâncias do zero. A opção E exige refatoração maciça.

es.scenario: Una aplicación de comercio financiero crítico se ejecuta en la región us-east-1. Depende de una base de datos Amazon RDS para PostgreSQL Multi-AZ y una flota de instancias EC2 administradas por un grupo de Auto Scaling detrás de un Application Load Balancer (ALB). El plan de continuidad dicta un RPO (Objetivo de Punto de Recuperación) de 5 minutos y un RTO (Objetivo de Tiempo de Recuperación) de menos de 15 minutos en caso de una interrupción regional. La empresa desea implementar una estrategia de DR en us-west-2 que cumpla estrictamente con estos objetivos y, al mismo tiempo, minimice los costos de infraestructura.
es.question: ¿Qué combinación de acciones debe tomar un Arquitecto de Soluciones para implementar esta estrategia? (Seleccione DOS.)

options.A: Configurar una réplica de lectura multirregión de Amazon RDS en us-west-2. En caso de desastre, promover la réplica a una instancia de base de datos independiente y actualizar las cadenas de conexión.
options.B: Habilitar AWS Backup para tomar instantáneas por hora de la instancia RDS y copiarlas a us-west-2. Restaurar la base de datos a partir de la instantánea más reciente en caso de desastre.
options.C: Implementar una arquitectura de Warm Standby en us-west-2 ejecutando un grupo de Auto Scaling reducido con capacidad mínima. Configurar Amazon Route 53 con enrutamiento de conmutación por error hacia el ALB en us-west-2.
options.D: Implementar una arquitectura Pilot Light en us-west-2 manteniendo la capacidad del grupo de Auto Scaling EC2 en cero. Depender de una función AWS Lambda para escalar las instancias durante un desastre.
options.E: Migrar la base de datos a Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables para garantizar una replicación sincrónica multirregión. Modificar la aplicación para usar DynamoDB en lugar de PostgreSQL.

es.explanation: Las opciones A y C son correctas. La réplica de lectura (A) cumple con el RPO de 5 minutos ya que replica en tiempo casi real. El Warm Standby (C) satisface el RTO de 15 minutos al tener instancias reducidas ya en ejecución. La opción B viola el RPO de 5 minutos. La opción D puede demorar más de 15 minutos en lanzar instancias desde cero. La opción E requeriría una refactorización masiva y sería excesivamente costosa.

en.scenario: A multinational corporation has accumulated petabytes of unstructured corporate data, including PDF reports, Word documents, and technical manuals. This data is scattered across on-premises Microsoft SharePoint servers and various Amazon S3 buckets. The Chief Knowledge Officer wants an intelligent search solution that allows employees to ask natural language questions (e.g., 'What is the standard procedure for onboarding a new vendor?') and receive highly accurate, context-aware answers directly extracted from the documents. The solution must support access control lists (ACLs) so employees only see results they are authorized to view.
en.question: Which solution meets these requirements with the LOWEST maintenance overhead?

options.A: Ingest all documents into Amazon OpenSearch Service. Develop a custom natural language processing pipeline using Amazon Comprehend to extract entities and build a searchable index. Synchronize the SharePoint ACLs using a custom AWS Lambda cron job that updates the OpenSearch document-level security policies.
options.B: Use Amazon Kendra to create an enterprise search index. Configure the native Amazon Kendra connectors for Amazon S3 and Microsoft SharePoint to continuously synchronize the documents. Enable the user access control feature in Amazon Kendra and pass user context tokens with each search request to enforce existing ACLs.
options.C: Use AWS Glue crawlers to catalog the metadata of all documents in an AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use Amazon Athena to query the metadata using standard SQL. Build a frontend application that translates natural language queries into SQL using Amazon Lex, and enforce document-level permissions using AWS Lake Formation.
options.D: Provision an Amazon EC2 instance fleet running Apache Solr. Use AWS DataSync to continuously replicate the SharePoint data to Amazon Elastic File System (EFS). Mount EFS on the Solr instances to index the data. Implement an AWS Directory Service AD Connector to handle user authentication and Solr row-level filtering.

en.explanation: Option B is correct. Amazon Kendra is a fully managed, ML-powered enterprise search service that natively supports natural language questions. It provides out-of-the-box data source connectors for SharePoint and S3, and natively supports enforcing Access Control Lists (ACLs) using user context tokens, representing the lowest maintenance overhead. Option A requires building complex custom ML pipelines and ACL synchronization. Option C uses Athena, which queries structured metadata, not unstructured PDF text. Option D is highly operational and lacks managed ML capabilities.

options.D: Provisionar uma frota do Amazon EC2 executando Apache Solr. Usar o AWS DataSync para replicar os dados do SharePoint para o Amazon EFS. Implementar um AD Connector para lidar com a autenticação de usuários e filtragem em nível de linha no Solr.

pt.explanation: A opção B está correta. O Amazon Kendra é um serviço de pesquisa corporativa alimentado por ML que suporta nativamente perguntas em linguagem natural. Ele fornece conectores nativos para SharePoint e S3 e suporta ACLs nativamente usando tokens de contexto de usuário. A opção A requer a construção de pipelines complexos de ML personalizados. A opção C usa Athena, que consulta metadados estruturados, não texto não estruturado em PDF. A opção D possui alta carga operacional.

en.scenario: An organization operates 80 AWS accounts, each containing a VPC. All VPCs are connected to a central AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) in a dedicated network account to facilitate communication. Recently, the networking team noticed a significant increase in data transfer costs. Analysis reveals that applications in Account A are frequently transferring terabytes of data to an Amazon S3 bucket located in Account B within the same AWS Region. Currently, the traffic routes through the Transit Gateway and uses the public S3 endpoints.
en.question: What is the MOST cost-effective architectural change to optimize the data transfer costs without compromising security or cross-account communication?

options.A: Create an AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint) for Amazon S3 in the Transit Gateway network account. Update the Route 53 Resolver rules to route S3 DNS queries through the TGW to the centralized interface endpoint.
options.B: Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for Amazon S3 directly within the VPC in Account A. Update the VPC route tables in Account A to route S3-bound traffic to the Gateway Endpoint instead of the Transit Gateway.
options.C: Configure a VPC Peering connection directly between the VPC in Account A and the VPC in Account B. Route all traffic between these two accounts over the peering connection instead of the Transit Gateway.
options.D: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket in Account B. Modify the applications in Account A to use the transfer acceleration endpoint to route traffic over the AWS global network backbone.

en.explanation: Option B is correct. Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 are completely free (no hourly charge, no data processing charge). By placing the Gateway Endpoint directly in Account A's VPC and updating the route table, the S3 traffic stays within the AWS network and entirely bypasses the Transit Gateway, eliminating TGW data processing costs and NAT/Egress costs. Option A uses Interface endpoints which incur hourly and per-GB processing fees. Option C is incorrect because S3 buckets do not reside in VPCs, so peering the two VPCs does not optimize traffic to the S3 public endpoint. Option D (S3 Transfer Acceleration) actually incurs additional charges per GB transferred.

pt.scenario: Uma organização opera 80 contas da AWS, cada uma contendo uma VPC. Todas as VPCs estão conectadas a um AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) central para facilitar a comunicação. A equipe de redes notou um aumento significativo nos custos de transferência de dados. A análise revela que aplicativos na Conta A estão frequentemente transferindo terabytes de dados para um bucket do Amazon S3 localizado na Conta B dentro da mesma região da AWS. Atualmente, o tráfego é roteado pelo Transit Gateway e usa os endpoints públicos do S3.
pt.question: Qual é a mudança arquitetônica MAIS econômica para otimizar os custos de transferência de dados sem comprometer a segurança ou a comunicação entre contas?

options.A: Criar um AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint) para o Amazon S3 na conta de rede do Transit Gateway. Atualizar as regras do Route 53 Resolver para rotear consultas DNS do S3 através do TGW para o endpoint de interface.
options.B: Criar um Gateway VPC Endpoint para o Amazon S3 diretamente na VPC na Conta A. Atualizar as tabelas de roteamento da VPC na Conta A para rotear o tráfego destinado ao S3 para o Gateway Endpoint em vez do Transit Gateway.
options.C: Configurar uma conexão de emparelhamento de VPC (VPC Peering) diretamente entre a VPC na Conta A e a VPC na Conta B. Rotear todo o tráfego entre essas duas contas pela conexão de emparelhamento em vez do Transit Gateway.
options.D: Ativar o Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration no bucket na Conta B. Modificar os aplicativos na Conta A para usar o endpoint de aceleração de transferência.

pt.explanation: A opção B está correta. Os Gateway VPC Endpoints para Amazon S3 são totalmente gratuitos. Ao colocar o Gateway Endpoint diretamente na VPC da Conta A, o tráfego do S3 contorna totalmente o Transit Gateway, eliminando os custos de processamento de dados do TGW. A opção A usa endpoints de Interface, que incorrem em taxas por hora e processamento por GB. A opção C é incorreta porque o S3 não reside em VPCs, portanto o peering não otimiza o acesso direto ao S3. A opção D gera custos adicionais por GB transferido.

es.scenario: Una organización opera 80 cuentas de AWS, cada una con una VPC. Todas las VPC están conectadas a un AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) central en una cuenta de red dedicada. El equipo de redes notó un aumento en los costos de transferencia de datos. El análisis revela que las aplicaciones en la Cuenta A transfieren con frecuencia terabytes de datos a un bucket de Amazon S3 en la Cuenta B dentro de la misma Región. Actualmente, el tráfico se enruta a través de TGW y utiliza los puntos de enlace públicos de S3.
es.question: ¿Cuál es el cambio arquitectónico MÁS rentable para optimizar los costos de transferencia de datos sin comprometer la seguridad?

options.A: Crear un AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint) para Amazon S3 en la cuenta del Transit Gateway. Actualizar las reglas de Route 53 Resolver para enrutar consultas de DNS de S3 a través del TGW hacia el punto de enlace de interfaz.
options.B: Crear un Gateway VPC Endpoint para Amazon S3 directamente dentro de la VPC en la Cuenta A. Actualizar las tablas de ruteo de la VPC en la Cuenta A para dirigir el tráfico con destino a S3 al Gateway Endpoint en lugar del Transit Gateway.
options.C: Configurar una conexión de VPC Peering directamente entre la VPC de la Cuenta A y la VPC de la Cuenta B. Enrutar todo el tráfico entre estas dos cuentas a través del peering en lugar del Transit Gateway.
options.D: Habilitar Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration en el bucket de la Cuenta B. Modificar las aplicaciones en la Cuenta A para utilizar el punto de enlace de aceleración de transferencia.

es.explanation: La opción B es correcta. Los Gateway VPC Endpoints para Amazon S3 son gratuitos. Al colocar el Endpoint directamente en la VPC de la Cuenta A, el tráfico de S3 evita el Transit Gateway, eliminando los costos de procesamiento de datos del TGW. La opción A utiliza puntos de enlace de Interfaz, que incurren en tarifas de procesamiento. La opción C es incorrecta porque los buckets de S3 no residen en VPC, por lo que el peering de VPC no optimiza el tráfico hacia S3. La opción D genera cargos adicionales por transferencia.

question.en: A company has an active Direct Connect (DX) connection and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection as a backup, both attached to a Transit Gateway (TGW). The on-premises router advertises the prefix 10.10.0.0/16 over DX and 10.10.0.0/24 over VPN. The company notices that traffic from AWS to on-premises is sometimes taking the VPN path instead of the preferred DX path. They want to ensure traffic always prefers the DX path, falling back to VPN only if DX goes down. Which actions will effectively ensure AWS routes traffic to on-premises via DX instead of VPN? (Select TWO.)
question.pt: Uma empresa tem uma conexão Direct Connect (DX) ativa e uma conexão AWS Site-to-Site VPN como backup, ambas anexadas a um Transit Gateway (TGW). O roteador on-premises anuncia o prefixo 10.10.0.0/16 sobre o DX e 10.10.0.0/24 sobre a VPN. A empresa percebe que o tráfego da AWS para on-premises às vezes está seguindo o caminho da VPN em vez do caminho preferencial do DX. Eles querem garantir que o tráfego sempre prefira o caminho do DX, usando a VPN apenas como fallback caso o DX caia. Quais ações garantirão efetivamente que a AWS roteie o tráfego para on-premises via DX em vez da VPN? (Selecione DUAS.)
question.es: Una empresa tiene una conexión Direct Connect (DX) activa y una conexión AWS Site-to-Site VPN como respaldo, ambas conectadas a un Transit Gateway (TGW). El enrutador local anuncia el prefijo 10.10.0.0/16 a través de DX y 10.10.0.0/24 a través de VPN. La empresa nota que el tráfico de AWS hacia las instalaciones locales a veces toma la ruta de la VPN en lugar de la ruta preferida de DX. Quieren asegurarse de que el tráfico siempre prefiera la ruta de DX, utilizando la VPN como respaldo solo si DX falla. ¿Qué acciones garantizarán efectivamente que AWS enrute el tráfico hacia las instalaciones locales a través de DX en lugar de VPN? (Seleccione DOS.)

text.en: Advertise the same 10.10.0.0/24 prefix over the DX connection. TGW automatically prefers the DX path over the VPN path when prefixes are identical.
text.pt: Anunciar o mesmo prefixo 10.10.0.0/24 sobre a conexão DX. O TGW prefere automaticamente o caminho do DX em vez da VPN quando os prefixos são idênticos.
text.es: Anunciar el mismo prefijo 10.10.0.0/24 a través de la conexión DX. El TGW prefiere automáticamente la ruta de DX sobre la de VPN cuando los prefijos son idénticos.

text.en: Summarize the VPN advertisement to 10.10.0.0/16. TGW evaluates identical prefixes by prioritizing Direct Connect attachments over VPN attachments.
text.pt: Resumir o anúncio da VPN para 10.10.0.0/16. O TGW avalia prefixos idênticos priorizando anexos do Direct Connect em vez de anexos de VPN.
text.es: Resumir el anuncio de VPN a 10.10.0.0/16. El TGW evalúa prefijos idénticos priorizando las conexiones de Direct Connect sobre las de VPN.

text.en: Configure AS PATH prepending on the DX connection to make the path shorter than the VPN connection.
text.pt: Configurar o 'AS PATH prepending' na conexão DX para tornar o caminho mais curto que a conexão VPN.
text.es: Configurar 'AS PATH prepending' en la conexión DX para hacer que la ruta sea más corta que la conexión VPN.

text.en: Configure Local Preference to a higher value on the on-premises router for the DX connection.
text.pt: Configurar a Preferência Local (Local Preference) para um valor mais alto no roteador on-premises para a conexão DX.
text.es: Configurar la Preferencia Local (Local Preference) a un valor más alto en el enrutador local para la conexión DX.

text.en: Modify the TGW route table to statically route 10.10.0.0/16 to the DX attachment, as static routes supersede BGP propagated routes.
text.pt: Modificar a tabela de rotas do TGW para rotear estaticamente 10.10.0.0/16 para o anexo do DX, pois as rotas estáticas substituem as rotas propagadas pelo BGP.
text.es: Modificar la tabla de rutas del TGW para enrutar estáticamente 10.10.0.0/16 al archivo adjunto de DX, ya que las rutas estáticas reemplazan las rutas propagadas por BGP.

explanation.en: AWS Transit Gateway routing strictly follows longest prefix match. Since the VPN was advertising a more specific prefix (/24) than DX (/16), traffic would traverse the VPN. To fix this, you must either make the DX prefix equally specific or make the VPN prefix less specific. When prefixes are identical, Transit Gateway inherently prefers Direct Connect paths over Site-to-Site VPN paths. AS PATH and Local Preference do not override longest prefix match rules.
explanation.pt: O roteamento do AWS Transit Gateway segue estritamente a correspondência de prefixo mais longo (longest prefix match). Como a VPN estava anunciando um prefixo mais específico (/24) do que o DX (/16), o tráfego atravessava a VPN. Para corrigir isso, você deve tornar o prefixo do DX igualmente específico ou tornar o prefixo da VPN menos específico. Quando os prefixos são idênticos, o Transit Gateway prefere inerentemente caminhos do Direct Connect em relação aos caminhos da Site-to-Site VPN. AS PATH e Local Preference não substituem as regras de correspondência de prefixo mais longo.
explanation.es: El enrutamiento de AWS Transit Gateway sigue estrictamente la coincidencia de prefijo más largo. Como la VPN anunciaba un prefijo más específico (/24) que DX (/16), el tráfico pasaba por la VPN. Para solucionarlo, debe hacer que el prefijo de DX sea igualmente específico o hacer que el prefijo de la VPN sea menos específico. Cuando los prefijos son idénticos, Transit Gateway prefiere intrínsecamente las rutas de Direct Connect sobre las de Site-to-Site VPN. AS PATH y Local Preference no anulan las reglas de coincidencia de prefijo más largo.

question.en: An enterprise has a shared services VPC in the us-east-1 region connected to an AWS Transit Gateway (TGW). A Route 53 Inbound Resolver endpoint and an Outbound Resolver endpoint reside in this VPC. On-premises DNS servers are connected via a Direct Connect connection terminating on a Direct Connect Gateway associated with the TGW. The on-premises servers need to resolve *.amazonaws.com domains (e.g., interface endpoints) in the VPCs, and the EC2 instances in all AWS VPCs need to resolve *.corp.local domains hosted on-premises. What must the Solutions Architect configure to enable this bi-directional DNS resolution? (Select THREE.)
question.pt: Uma empresa possui uma VPC de serviços compartilhados na região us-east-1 conectada a um AWS Transit Gateway (TGW). Um endpoint Inbound e um Outbound do Route 53 Resolver residem nesta VPC. Servidores DNS on-premises estão conectados via Direct Connect terminando em um Direct Connect Gateway associado ao TGW. Os servidores on-premises precisam resolver domínios *.amazonaws.com nas VPCs, e as instâncias EC2 em todas as VPCs da AWS precisam resolver domínios *.corp.local hospedados on-premises. O que o Arquiteto de Soluções deve configurar para habilitar essa resolução de DNS bidirecional? (Selecione TRÊS.)
question.es: Una empresa tiene una VPC de servicios compartidos en la región us-east-1 conectada a un AWS Transit Gateway (TGW). Un endpoint Inbound y un Outbound de Route 53 Resolver residen en esta VPC. Los servidores DNS locales están conectados a través de Direct Connect que termina en un Direct Connect Gateway asociado al TGW. Los servidores locales necesitan resolver dominios *.amazonaws.com en las VPC, y las instancias EC2 en todas las VPC de AWS necesitan resolver dominios *.corp.local alojados de forma local. ¿Qué debe configurar el Arquitecto de Soluciones para habilitar esta resolución de DNS bidireccional? (Seleccione TRES.)

text.en: Create a Route 53 Resolver forwarding rule for corp.local that points to the on-premises DNS server IPs using the Outbound Resolver endpoint. Associate this rule with all applicable VPCs.
text.pt: Criar uma regra de encaminhamento do Route 53 Resolver para corp.local que aponte para os IPs dos servidores DNS on-premises usando o endpoint Outbound. Associar esta regra a todas as VPCs aplicáveis.
text.es: Crear una regla de reenvío de Route 53 Resolver para corp.local que apunte a las IP de los servidores DNS locales mediante el endpoint Outbound. Asociar esta regla con todas las VPC aplicables.

text.en: On the on-premises DNS servers, configure a conditional forwarder for amazonaws.com pointing to the IP addresses of the Route 53 Inbound Resolver endpoint.
text.pt: Nos servidores DNS on-premises, configurar um encaminhador condicional (conditional forwarder) para amazonaws.com apontando para os endereços IP do endpoint Inbound do Route 53 Resolver.
text.es: En los servidores DNS locales, configurar un reenviador condicional para amazonaws.com que apunte a las direcciones IP del endpoint Inbound de Route 53 Resolver.

text.en: Configure the on-premises router to advertise the on-premises DNS server IP subnets over the DX connection so the Outbound Resolver can reach them via the TGW.
text.pt: Configurar o roteador on-premises para anunciar as sub-redes IP dos servidores DNS on-premises através da conexão DX, para que o Outbound Resolver possa alcançá-los via TGW.
text.es: Configurar el enrutador local para que anuncie las subredes IP de los servidores DNS locales a través de la conexión DX para que el Outbound Resolver pueda acceder a ellos a través del TGW.

text.en: Create a Route 53 Private Hosted Zone for corp.local and associate it with the shared services VPC to cache on-premises records.
text.pt: Criar uma Hosted Zone privada no Route 53 para corp.local e associá-la à VPC de serviços compartilhados para armazenar registros on-premises em cache.
text.es: Crear una Hosted Zone privada en Route 53 para corp.local y asociarla con la VPC de servicios compartidos para almacenar en caché los registros locales.

text.en: Enable DNS Hostnames and DNS Resolution on the Direct Connect Gateway.
text.pt: Habilitar Nomes de Host DNS e Resolução DNS no Direct Connect Gateway.
text.es: Habilitar Nombres de Host DNS y Resolución DNS en el Direct Connect Gateway.

text.en: Create a Route 53 Resolver rule for amazonaws.com and associate it with the on-premises network CIDR.
text.pt: Criar uma regra do Route 53 Resolver para amazonaws.com e associá-la ao CIDR da rede on-premises.
text.es: Crear una regla de Route 53 Resolver para amazonaws.com y asociarla con el CIDR de la red local.

explanation.en: To resolve on-premises domains from AWS, a Route 53 Outbound Resolver endpoint is used alongside a forwarding rule targeting the on-premises DNS servers. The on-premises network must also be reachable, requiring proper BGP advertisement of the DNS server subnets over DX. To resolve AWS domains from on-premises, a conditional forwarder is created on the on-premises DNS servers pointing to the Inbound Resolver endpoint IPs. DX Gateways do not have DNS attributes to toggle.
explanation.pt: Para resolver domínios on-premises a partir da AWS, um endpoint Outbound do Route 53 Resolver é usado com uma regra de encaminhamento para os servidores DNS on-premises. A rede on-premises deve ser acessível, exigindo o anúncio BGP adequado via DX. Para resolver domínios da AWS do on-premises, um encaminhador condicional é criado nos servidores DNS apontando para os IPs do endpoint Inbound. DX Gateways não possuem atributos DNS para alternar.
explanation.es: Para resolver dominios locales desde AWS, se utiliza un endpoint Outbound de Route 53 Resolver junto con una regla de reenvío dirigida a los servidores DNS locales. La red local también debe ser accesible, lo que requiere un anuncio BGP adecuado a través de DX. Para resolver dominios de AWS desde las instalaciones locales, se crea un reenviador condicional en los servidores DNS locales que apunta a las direcciones IP del endpoint Inbound. Los Gateways DX no tienen atributos de DNS.

question.en: A gaming company deployed a multiplayer game server fleet in two AWS Regions (us-west-2 and eu-central-1) behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs). The game uses a custom UDP protocol for real-time game state synchronization and a TCP protocol for authentication. The company wants to minimize global latency, ensure extremely fast failover if a region degrades, and retain the clients' source IP addresses on the game servers. Which solution meets these requirements? (Select ONE.)
question.pt: Uma empresa de jogos implantou uma frota de servidores de jogos multiplayer em duas regiões da AWS (us-west-2 e eu-central-1) atrás de Network Load Balancers (NLBs). O jogo usa um protocolo UDP personalizado para sincronização e um protocolo TCP para autenticação. A empresa deseja minimizar a latência global, garantir um failover extremamente rápido se uma região degradar e reter os endereços IP de origem dos clientes nos servidores de jogos. Qual solução atende a esses requisitos? (Selecione UMA.)
question.es: Una empresa de juegos implementó una flota de servidores en dos regiones de AWS (us-west-2 y eu-central-1) detrás de Network Load Balancers (NLBs). El juego utiliza un protocolo UDP personalizado para sincronización y un protocolo TCP para autenticación. La empresa desea minimizar la latencia global, garantizar una conmutación por error extremadamente rápida si una región se degrada y retener las IP de origen de los clientes en los servidores. ¿Qué solución cumple con estos requisitos? (Seleccione UNA.)

text.en: Use AWS Global Accelerator with the two NLBs as endpoint groups. Configure listeners for both UDP and TCP. The client IPs are preserved by default when NLBs are the endpoints.
text.pt: Usar o AWS Global Accelerator com os dois NLBs como grupos de endpoints. Configurar listeners para UDP e TCP. Os IPs dos clientes são preservados por padrão quando os NLBs são os endpoints.
text.es: Usar AWS Global Accelerator con los dos NLB como grupos de endpoints. Configurar listeners para UDP y TCP. Las IP de los clientes se conservan de forma predeterminada cuando los NLB son los endpoints.

text.en: Use Amazon CloudFront with the two NLBs as custom origins. CloudFront will pass the client IP in the X-Forwarded-For header for TCP, and use a custom UDP behavior for the game state.
text.pt: Usar o Amazon CloudFront com os dois NLBs como origens personalizadas. O CloudFront passará o IP do cliente no cabeçalho X-Forwarded-For para TCP e usará um comportamento UDP personalizado.
text.es: Usar Amazon CloudFront con los dos NLB como orígenes personalizados. CloudFront pasará la IP del cliente en el encabezado X-Forwarded-For para TCP, y usará un comportamiento UDP personalizado.

text.en: Use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to direct clients to the closest NLB. Enable cross-zone load balancing on the NLBs to preserve client IP.
text.pt: Usar o roteamento baseado em latência do Amazon Route 53 para direcionar clientes ao NLB mais próximo. Habilitar o balanceamento de carga cross-zone nos NLBs para preservar o IP do cliente.
text.es: Usar el enrutamiento basado en latencia de Amazon Route 53 para dirigir a los clientes al NLB más cercano. Habilitar el balanceo de carga cross-zone en los NLB para preservar la IP del cliente.

text.en: Use AWS Global Accelerator with Application Load Balancers (ALBs) instead of NLBs. Enable the preserve client IP option in Global Accelerator.
text.pt: Usar o AWS Global Accelerator com Application Load Balancers (ALBs) em vez de NLBs. Habilitar a opção de preservar IP do cliente no Global Accelerator.
text.es: Usar AWS Global Accelerator con Application Load Balancers (ALB) en lugar de NLB. Habilitar la opción de conservar IP de cliente en Global Accelerator.

explanation.en: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to route traffic to the optimal region based on performance, bypassing the public internet's congestion. It natively supports both TCP and UDP protocols, which is critical for the custom game state protocol. When targeting Network Load Balancers (NLBs), Global Accelerator preserves the client's source IP address without requiring extra headers. CloudFront and ALBs do not support arbitrary UDP protocols. Route 53 failover relies on DNS TTLs, which is slower than Global Accelerator's Anycast IP failover.
explanation.pt: O AWS Global Accelerator usa a rede global da AWS para rotear o tráfego para a região ideal com base no desempenho, contornando o congestionamento da internet pública. Ele suporta nativamente os protocolos TCP e UDP, o que é fundamental para o protocolo de jogo personalizado. Ao usar NLBs como alvo, o Global Accelerator preserva o endereço IP de origem do cliente sem exigir cabeçalhos extras. CloudFront e ALBs não suportam protocolos UDP arbitrários. O failover do Route 53 depende de DNS TTLs, que é mais lento que o Anycast do Global Accelerator.
explanation.es: AWS Global Accelerator utiliza la red global de AWS para enrutar el tráfico a la región óptima según el rendimiento, evitando la congestión de Internet público. Admite de forma nativa los protocolos TCP y UDP, lo cual es fundamental para el protocolo de juego. Al dirigirse a los NLB, Global Accelerator conserva la dirección IP de origen del cliente sin requerir encabezados adicionales. CloudFront y ALB no admiten protocolos UDP arbitrarios. La conmutación por error de Route 53 depende de los DNS TTL, que es más lento que Anycast de Global Accelerator.

questions.domain: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

question.en: A SaaS provider exposes a secure data processing application using AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) in the us-east-1 region. An enterprise customer wants to consume this service directly from their on-premises data center. The customer has a Direct Connect (DX) connection terminating at a Direct Connect Gateway, which is attached to a Transit Gateway (TGW). The TGW is routed to the customer's VPC in us-east-1. How can the customer securely access the SaaS application using private IP addresses from on-premises? (Select TWO.)
question.pt: Um provedor de SaaS expõe um aplicativo seguro de processamento de dados usando AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) na região us-east-1. Um cliente corporativo deseja consumir este serviço diretamente de seu data center on-premises. O cliente possui uma conexão Direct Connect (DX) terminando em um Direct Connect Gateway, anexado a um Transit Gateway (TGW). O TGW está roteado para a VPC do cliente em us-east-1. Como o cliente pode acessar o aplicativo SaaS com segurança usando IPs privados on-premises? (Selecione DUAS.)
question.es: Un proveedor de SaaS expone una aplicación segura de procesamiento de datos utilizando AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) en la región us-east-1. Un cliente corporativo desea consumir este servicio directamente desde su centro de datos local. El cliente tiene una conexión Direct Connect (DX) que termina en un Direct Connect Gateway conectado a un Transit Gateway (TGW). El TGW está enrutado a la VPC del cliente en us-east-1. ¿Cómo puede el cliente acceder de forma segura a la aplicación SaaS utilizando IP privadas locales? (Seleccione DOS.)

text.en: The customer creates a VPC Interface Endpoint for the SaaS provider's Endpoint Service inside their us-east-1 VPC.
text.pt: O cliente cria um VPC Interface Endpoint para o Endpoint Service do provedor SaaS dentro de sua VPC em us-east-1.
text.es: El cliente crea un VPC Interface Endpoint para el Endpoint Service del proveedor SaaS dentro de su VPC en us-east-1.

text.en: The customer routes traffic from on-premises over a Private VIF to the Direct Connect Gateway, then through the TGW to the VPC where the Interface Endpoint is located.
text.pt: O cliente roteia o tráfego do on-premises por um Private VIF para o Direct Connect Gateway, depois pelo TGW até a VPC onde o Interface Endpoint está localizado.
text.es: El cliente enruta el tráfico desde las instalaciones locales a través de un Private VIF al Direct Connect Gateway, luego a través del TGW a la VPC donde se encuentra el Interface Endpoint.

text.en: The customer creates a Public VIF on their DX connection to directly access the SaaS provider's AWS PrivateLink endpoint over the AWS backbone.
text.pt: O cliente cria um Public VIF em sua conexão DX para acessar diretamente o endpoint AWS PrivateLink do provedor SaaS pelo backbone da AWS.
text.es: El cliente crea un Public VIF en su conexión DX para acceder directamente al endpoint de AWS PrivateLink del proveedor SaaS a través de la red troncal de AWS.

text.en: The SaaS provider configures the Endpoint Service to add the customer's on-premises IP CIDR range to the allowed principals list.
text.pt: O provedor SaaS configura o Endpoint Service para adicionar a faixa de IP CIDR do on-premises do cliente à lista de principais permitidos.
text.es: El proveedor de SaaS configura el Endpoint Service para agregar el rango CIDR IP local del cliente a la lista de entidades principales permitidas.

text.en: The customer configures an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the DX connection because AWS PrivateLink traffic originating from on-premises mandates IPsec encryption.
text.pt: O cliente configura uma conexão AWS Site-to-Site VPN sobre a conexão DX porque o tráfego do AWS PrivateLink originado do on-premises exige criptografia IPsec.
text.es: El cliente configura una conexión AWS Site-to-Site VPN sobre la conexión DX porque el tráfico de AWS PrivateLink originado localmente requiere cifrado IPsec.

explanation.en: AWS PrivateLink enables consumption of services securely over private IPs by deploying an Interface Endpoint in a customer VPC. On-premises environments can access these Interface Endpoints by routing traffic over an AWS Direct Connect connection (using a Private VIF or Transit VIF) or an AWS VPN connection to the VPC containing the endpoint. The allowed principals for PrivateLink are IAM ARNs, not IP ranges. Public VIFs are for reaching AWS public endpoints (like Amazon S3 public IPs), not PrivateLink endpoints.
explanation.pt: O AWS PrivateLink permite o consumo de serviços de forma segura por IPs privados ao implantar um Interface Endpoint em uma VPC do cliente. explanation.en: In a dual-stack VPC, IPv4 and IPv6 traffic are handled independently. For IPv4 instances in private subnets to access the internet securely (outbound only), a NAT Gateway is deployed in a public subnet. For IPv6, the architecture is different because all IPv6 addresses are globally routable. Instead of NAT, AWS provides an Egress-Only Internet Gateway, which allows outbound IPv6 traffic to the internet but inherently blocks any inbound IPv6 traffic initiated from the internet. Using an Internet Gateway (IGW) for IPv6 in a private subnet would technically allow inbound traffic if not perfectly restricted by Security Groups and NACLs, violating the strict requirement.

explanation.es: En una VPC dual-stack, el tráfico IPv4 e IPv6 se maneja de forma independiente. questions.statement: An enterprise with a multi-account strategy based on AWS Organizations needs to deploy an AWS Config rule to all current and future accounts within specific Organizational Units (OUs). The architecture board requires a zero-maintenance approach where new accounts automatically inherit the rule upon creation, and the deployment must span multiple AWS Regions.

options.text: Create a CloudFormation StackSet using self-managed permissions. Trigger an AWS Lambda function via Amazon EventBridge on the CreateAccount event to manually deploy the stack instance to the newly created account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed permissions require manual trust setup, and relying on EventBridge + Lambda adds unnecessary operational overhead compared to native features.

options.text: Create a CloudFormation StackSet using service-managed permissions and enable automatic deployments. Target the deployment directly to the specific Organizational Units (OUs) within AWS Organizations.
options.explanation: Correct: Service-managed StackSets integrate natively with AWS Organizations, automatically deploying stacks to new accounts in targeted OUs without custom automation.

options.text: Write an AWS CloudFormation template and deploy it using AWS Systems Manager State Manager across all accounts. Use EventBridge to trigger it for new accounts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Systems Manager can run scripts, CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions is the native, purpose-built feature for this cross-account declarative deployment.

options.text: Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory to run a custom CloudFormation template for new accounts, and manually deploy the template to existing accounts using an AWS CodePipeline.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This approach splits the deployment logic (Control Tower for new, Pipeline for existing), violating the zero-maintenance and unified management requirement.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions allow you to centrally manage deployments to AWS accounts within AWS Organizations. By enabling automatic deployments, StackSets automatically deploys to any new account added to the target OUs.

questions.statement: A company employs a microservices architecture. The central networking team provisions the VPC, Subnets, and Security Groups using a CloudFormation template. Multiple application teams need to reference the VPC ID and Subnet IDs dynamically in their own CloudFormation templates. The networking resources must be protected from accidental deletion if an app team deletes their stack, and the networking lifecycle must remain strictly decoupled from the applications.

options.text: Use CloudFormation Nested Stacks. Have the networking team create a parent stack and reference the app teams' templates as AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resources to pass the VPC parameters down.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Nested stacks tightly couple the lifecycles together. If the root stack is deleted, all nested stacks are deleted, which violates the decoupling requirement.

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. The networking team writes the IDs as standard Strings. App teams use the resolve:ssm dynamic reference to fetch the IDs, while depending on CloudFormation deletion policies to prevent VPC deletion.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While SSM can share data, it does not natively prevent the deletion of the networking resources if someone manually tries to delete them or if dependencies are complex.

options.text: The networking team's template should use the Outputs section with the Export field to export the IDs. The app teams' templates should use the Fn::ImportValue intrinsic function to reference the network resources.
options.explanation: Correct: Cross-stack references (Outputs/Export and Fn::ImportValue) prevent the networking stack from being deleted or modified in ways that break the exported values while another stack is actively referencing them.

options.text: Use CloudFormation Custom Resources backed by AWS Lambda in the app templates to query the EC2 API and retrieve the VPC ID and Subnet IDs dynamically based on tags.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Custom Resources add unnecessary complexity and Lambda maintenance when native cross-stack references securely solve the problem and enforce dependency protection.

questions.generalExplanation: Cross-stack references let you export values from one stack and import them into another using the Export field and Fn::ImportValue. CloudFormation enforces tight referential integrity: you cannot delete a stack if another stack is importing its exported values.

Os recursos de rede devem ser protegidos contra exclusão acidental caso uma equipe de aplicativo exclua sua stack, e o ciclo de vida da rede deve permanecer estritamente desacoplado dos aplicativos.

options.text: Usar CloudFormation Nested Stacks. A equipe de rede cria uma stack pai e referencia os templates das equipes de app como recursos AWS::CloudFormation::Stack para repassar os parâmetros da VPC.

options.text: Usar CloudFormation Custom Resources respaldados por AWS Lambda en las plantillas de las aplicaciones para consultar la API de EC2 y recuperar el ID de la VPC y de las Subredes dinámicamente en función de etiquetas.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: An operations team is deploying an application via an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling Group using CloudFormation. The instances require a complex software installation upon boot that takes 10 minutes. The team must ensure that CloudFormation pauses the stack creation and only marks the instances as successfully created after the software is fully configured. Furthermore, if configuration files within the CloudFormation template are updated later, the instances must apply the new configuration dynamically without terminating or replacing the underlying EC2 instances. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use the cfn-signal helper script in the UserData section to send a success signal to a CreationPolicy attached to the Auto Scaling Group once the application software installation is complete.
options.explanation: Correct: The CreationPolicy ensures CloudFormation waits for a specified number of success signals (sent via cfn-signal) before moving the ASG resource to the CREATE_COMPLETE state.

options.text: Define the software installation in the AWS::CloudFormation::Init metadata of the Launch Template. Install and configure the cfn-hup daemon on the instances to detect metadata changes and re-run the configuration scripts automatically.
options.explanation: Correct: cfn-hup periodically polls the CloudFormation API for updates to the logical resource's AWS::CloudFormation::Init metadata and triggers the cfn-init actions to apply configuration changes dynamically without instance replacement.

options.text: Attach a WaitCondition resource to the Launch Template and use a presigned URL in the UserData script to send a signal when the installation succeeds.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While WaitConditions can pause execution, for Auto Scaling groups and EC2 instances, AWS explicitly recommends using a CreationPolicy instead of a WaitCondition for better integration and simpler templates.

options.text: Set the UpdatePolicy attribute on the Auto Scaling Group to AutoScalingRollingUpdate with a PauseTime of 15 minutes to allow configuration updates.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AutoScalingRollingUpdate actually terminates and replaces EC2 instances to deploy the update, which explicitly violates the requirement of NOT replacing the underlying instances.

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command triggered by an EventBridge rule matching CloudFormation update events to reinstall the software and signal the Auto Scaling group.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This is an overly complex, non-native approach. CloudFormation natively provides cfn-init and cfn-hup precisely for this desired state configuration pattern.

questions.generalExplanation: To delay resource completion during boot, a CreationPolicy coupled with cfn-signal ensures the Auto Scaling group waits until the software is ready. For dynamic in-place updates, defining desired state in AWS::CloudFormation::Init and running the cfn-hup daemon allows instances to detect template metadata changes and apply them without requiring instance termination.
